|strategy=By [mailto:zube@eagle.cc.ukans.edu Nick Zube]<ref name="decipher-strategy">https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/light/small/ajedisresilience.html</ref>

Sometimes, things go very, very wrong.

Like when [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] Epic Duels Jedi [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]]...and wins.

Now you're faced with a choice: Lose 6 Force and give your opponent one of your best characters, or lose 18 Force &#150; and [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]]. I hate choices like that.

Thanks to [[A Jedi's Resilience]], I don't have to make them anymore.

This 6-destiny Interrupt can be the card that saves you the game. When you do your best to win a duel, but it's not quite enough, [[A Jedi's Resilience]] spares you the agony of defeat by canceling the duel &#150; which gives you enough time to take a nice, long drink of your favorite beverage to calm your anxious nerves. Now, mind you, the danger isn't over; since the opponent's duel-initiating Interrupt (if any) goes back to his or her hand, the duel can happen again next turn. So you'd better use your brief respite to get the heck outta dodge before [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] calls [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]] out again. On the plus side, you can use it to make [[Darth Maul]] lose 1 Force for no reason at all.

But even if you don't fear duels, [[A Jedi's Resilience]] has a smooth secondary function: if you lose a character armed with a lightsaber, just do the ol' switcheroo to take the character right back into your hand. The fact that most lightsaber-wielding characters have super-high forfeit values does not go unnoticed when it comes time to forfeit...

If [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]]'s just about to be turned to the Dark Side, you'll be glad he's tough as a roach.

Since these characters have built-in sabers, you don't lose the weapon when you take them back into your hand... and you're ready to deploy them again.
